record_title: Sharp minimax relaxation frontier for scalar Newton under derivative-sector bounds
scientific_context: For scalar C1 root finding with global derivative bounds 0<m<=f'<=L, the record gives the exact worst one-step root-error envelope for constant-relaxation Newton, the optimal constant damping and factor, a sharp kappa=2 global-convergence boundary with explicit two-cycles for every kappa>2, and a minimax theorem showing that optimal derivative-dependent multiplicative relaxation cancels the Newton denominator and becomes the standard fixed-slope iteration.
limitations: Scalar real equations, exact arithmetic, global C1 derivative-sector bounds, and root error only. The derivative-aware minimax class is memoryless multiplicative relaxation based on the current derivative and known m,L; systems, line searches, trust regions, finite precision and history-dependent algorithms are outside scope. The sufficient damping inequality gamma<2m/L has prior coverage in more general damped-Newton theory and is not claimed as new. Older relaxation literature leaves residual historical-equivalence uncertainty.
